question:
Which of the following group elements are called chalcogens?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Group-16
Group-2
Group-17
Group-18
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Group-16

Explanation:
The elements of Group-16 in the periodic table are called chalcogens. This group includes oxygen (O), sulfur (S), selenium (Se), tellurium (Te), and polonium (Po). The name "chalcogen" is derived from the Greek words "chalcos" (ore) and "gen" (producer), as these elements are often found in metal ores. They have six electrons in their outermost shell, leading to a -2 oxidation state. Elements like oxygen and sulfur are crucial for life and industrial applications.

Extra Facts:
☛ Oxygen is the most abundant element on Earth and a major component of water (H2O).
☛ Sulfur is used in gunpowder, fertilizers, and the vulcanization of rubber.
☛ Selenium is used in photocopiers and solar cells.
☛ Polonium is a radioactive element used in nuclear reactors.

question:
______ are known as electronegative elements because they form negatively charged ions by the gain of electrons.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Non- metals
Alloys
Compounds
Mixtures
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Non-metals

Explanation:
Non-metals are known as electronegative elements because they form negatively charged ions (anions) by gaining electrons. Non-metals have a high tendency to gain electrons as their outer shell contains 4-7 electrons, and they complete their octet by accepting electrons. For example, chlorine (Cl) is a non-metal that gains one electron to form a Cl⁻ ion. This property makes non-metals electronegative, whereas metals lose electrons to form positively charged ions (cations).

Extra Facts:
Electronegativity is the ability of an element to attract electrons towards itself. Fluorine (F) is the most electronegative element. Non-metals are generally gases (e.g., oxygen, nitrogen) or solids (e.g., sulfur, phosphorus) and are poor conductors of electricity, except graphite, which is a good conductor. Non-metals form acidic oxides that dissolve in water to give acids, e.g., SO₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₃ (sulfurous acid).

☛ What is the formula of chloride ion? → Cl⁻
☛ Non-metals are generally _____ of electricity. → Poor conductors (except graphite)
☛ What type of ions do metals form? → Positively charged (cations)
☛ What type of oxides do non-metals form? → Acidic oxides
question_hi:
________ को विद्युत ऋणात्मक तत्व के रूप में जाना जाता है क्योंकि वे इलेक्ट्रॉनों के ग्रहण से ऋणावेशित आयन बनाते हैं।

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: अधातु
मिश्र धातु
यौगिक
मिश्रण
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है अधातु

Explanation:
अधातु को विद्युत ऋणात्मक तत्व के रूप में जाना जाता है क्योंकि वे इलेक्ट्रॉनों को ग्रहण करके ऋणावेशित आयन (ऐनायन) बनाते हैं। अधातुओं में इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण करने की प्रवृत्ति अधिक होती है क्योंकि उनके बाहरी कोश में 4-7 इलेक्ट्रॉन होते हैं और वे अष्टक को पूरा करने के लिए इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण करते हैं। उदाहरण के लिए, क्लोरीन (Cl) एक अधातु है जो एक इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण करके Cl⁻ आयन बनाता है। यह गुण अधातुओं को विद्युत ऋणात्मक बनाता है, जबकि धातुएँ इलेक्ट्रॉनों को त्यागकर धनावेशित आयन (कैटायन) बनाती हैं।

Extra Facts:
विद्युत ऋणात्मकता एक तत्व की इलेक्ट्रॉनों को अपनी ओर आकर्षित करने की क्षमता है। फ्लोरीन (F) सबसे अधिक विद्युत ऋणात्मक तत्व है। अधातुएँ आमतौर पर गैसें (जैसे ऑक्सीजन, नाइट्रोजन) या ठोस (जैसे सल्फर, फॉस्फोरस) होती हैं और विद्युत की कुचालक होती हैं, लेकिन ग्रेफाइट एक अपवाद है जो विद्युत का सुचालक है। अधातुएँ अम्लीय ऑक्साइड बनाती हैं जो पानी में घुलकर अम्ल देते हैं, जैसे SO₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₃ (सल्फ्यूरस अम्ल)।

question:
Identify the element one that does NOT belong to Group 1 of the Modern Periodic Table.

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Sodium
Lithium
Hydrogen
Rubidium
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Hydrogen

Explanation:
Group 1 of the Modern Periodic Table consists of Alkali Metals, which include Lithium (Li), Sodium (Na), Potassium (K), Rubidium (Rb), Cesium (Cs), and Francium (Fr). These metals have 1 electron in their outermost shell, making them highly reactive.

Hydrogen (H) also has 1 electron in its outer shell, but it is a non-metal and exhibits different properties compared to alkali metals. Although hydrogen is placed in Group 1, it is technically not an alkali metal. Hence, it does not belong to the alkali metal category despite being in Group 1.

Extra Facts:
- Hydrogen holds a unique position in the periodic table as it is neither a true metal nor a non-metal.
- Alkali metals react with water to form alkaline solutions, whereas hydrogen does not.
- Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe and serves as the primary fuel for nuclear fusion in stars.
- Alkali metals are stored in oil to prevent rapid reactions with air and moisture.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams

☛ Which group do alkali metals belong to? → Group 1
☛ Which is the most reactive metal? → Francium
☛ What is the atomic number of hydrogen? → 1
☛ What do alkali metals form with water? → Alkaline solutions
question_hi:

[SSC CGL 2023]
options_hi: सोडियम
लीथियम
हाइड्रोजन
रूबिडियम
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है हाइड्रोजन

Explanation:
आधुनिक आवर्त सारणी के समूह 1 में क्षार धातुएँ (Alkali Metals) शामिल हैं, जिनमें लीथियम (Li), सोडियम (Na), पोटैशियम (K), रूबिडियम (Rb), सीज़ियम (Cs) और फ्रैंशियम (Fr) आते हैं। ये सभी धातुएँ हैं और इनके बाहरी कोश में 1 इलेक्ट्रॉन होता है, जिसके कारण ये अत्यधिक अभिक्रियाशील होती हैं।

हाइड्रोजन (H) भी अपने बाहरी कोश में 1 इलेक्ट्रॉन रखता है, लेकिन यह एक अधातु (Non-Metal) है और इसके गुण क्षार धातुओं से भिन्न हैं। हाइड्रोजन को समूह 1 में रखा गया है, लेकिन यह तकनीकी रूप से क्षार धातु नहीं है। इसलिए, यह समूह 1 का सदस्य होते हुए भी क्षार धातुओं की श्रेणी में नहीं आता।

Extra Facts:
- हाइड्रोजन आवर्त सारणी में एक अनोखा स्थान रखता है क्योंकि यह न तो पूर्णतः धातु है और न ही अधातु।
- क्षार धातुएँ जल के साथ अभिक्रिया करके क्षारीय घोल (Alkaline Solution) बनाती हैं, जबकि हाइड्रोजन ऐसा नहीं करता।
- हाइड्रोजन ब्रह्मांड में सबसे प्रचुर तत्व है और यह सितारों (Stars) में नाभिकीय संलयन (Nuclear Fusion) का प्रमुख ईंधन है।
- क्षार धातुओं को तेल में डुबोकर रखा जाता है क्योंकि ये वायु और जल के साथ तेजी से अभिक्रिया करती हैं।

question:
In which year did John Alexander Newlands propound a new concept of the ‘Law of Octaves' proposing the periodicity of chemical elements arranged in order of atomic weight?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: 1860
1865
1873
1870
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1865

Explanation:
John Alexander Newlands proposed the Law of Octaves in 1865. He observed that when elements were arranged in order of increasing atomic weight, every eighth element had properties similar to the first, similar to the repetition of the eighth note in music. This concept later became the foundation for Mendeleev’s Periodic Law. However, Newlands' law was only applicable up to calcium and failed with newly discovered elements.

Extra Facts:
- Newlands presented his law to the Royal Society of Chemistry in 1866, but it was not recognized.
- Mendeleev proposed his periodic table in 1869, arranging elements based on atomic weight and chemical properties.
- The modern periodic table is based on atomic number, proposed by Henry Moseley in 1913.

जॉन एलेक्जेंडर न्यूलैंड्स ने 1865 में 'अष्टक के नियम' (Law of Octaves) का प्रस्ताव रखा। उन्होंने देखा कि जब तत्वों को उनके परमाणु भार के बढ़ते क्रम में व्यवस्थित किया जाता है, तो हर आठवें तत्व के गुण पहले तत्व के समान होते हैं, जैसे संगीत के सुरों में आठवें सुर की पुनरावृत्ति होती है। यह अवधारणा बाद में मेंडलीफ के आवर्त नियम (Mendeleev’s Periodic Law) का आधार बनी। हालांकि, न्यूलैंड्स का नियम केवल कैल्शियम तक ही लागू होता था और नए खोजे गए तत्वों के साथ असफल रहा।

Extra Facts:
- न्यूलैंड्स ने अपने नियम को 1866 में रॉयल सोसाइटी ऑफ केमिस्ट्री के समक्ष प्रस्तुत किया, लेकिन इसे मान्यता नहीं मिली।

- आधुनिक आवर्त सारणी परमाणु संख्या (Atomic Number) पर आधारित है, जिसे हेनरी मोस्ले ने 1913 में प्रस्तावित किया था।

question:
Which radioactive element with atomic number 43 in the modern periodic table is unstable, and the half-lives of all its isotopes are relatively short, from 4.2 million years to 5.0 s ?

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: Promethium
Nobelium
Technetium
Neptunium
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Technetium

Explanation:
Technetium (Tc) is a radioactive element with atomic number 43 in the modern periodic table. It is the first artificially produced element and is found in very small quantities in nature. All isotopes of technetium are unstable, with half-lives ranging from 4.2 million years (Tc-98) to 5.0 seconds (Tc-108). This element is located in the d-block and has an electronic configuration of [Kr] 4d5 5s2. Technetium is used in the medical field for radioisotope imaging, particularly in heart and bone scans.

Extra Facts:
Technetium was discovered in 1937 by Carlo Perrier and Emilio Segrè. It is a transition metal, and its name is derived from the Greek word 'technetos,' meaning 'artificial.' Technetium-99m (Tc-99m) is the most widely used radioisotope in medicine because it emits gamma rays and has a half-life of only 6 hours, making it safe for patients.

question:
The correct electronic configuration of Cu is :

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options:
[Ar] 3d⁹ 4s²

[Ar] 3d⁸ 4s² 4p¹

[Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s²

[Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is [Ar] 3d10 4s1

Explanation:
Copper (Cu) has an atomic number of 29. Its electronic configuration is [Ar] 3d10 4s1, not [Ar] 3d9 4s2. This occurs because a completely or half-filled d-orbital provides greater stability. In copper, filling the 3d subshell completely (10 electrons) and the 4s subshell half (1 electron) results in more stability. This is an example of an 'exceptional electronic configuration,' observed in elements like chromium (Cr) and copper (Cu). It aligns with Hund's rule and the Aufbau principle, which explain how electrons are distributed to achieve maximum stability in electronic configurations.

Extra Facts:
Copper (Cu) is a transition metal located in the d-block. It is used in electrical conductors, coins, and various alloys. Copper's electronic configuration is an exception because it does not follow the general electron-filling rule. A similar exception is seen in chromium (Cr), whose electronic configuration is [Ar] 3d5 4s1. These exceptions occur to achieve greater stability in electronic configurations, made possible by completely or half-filled subshells.

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Neither I nor II
Both I and II

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Neither I nor II

Explanation:
Valency is the combining capacity of an element to form chemical bonds. Boron (B) has a valency of 3, not 2, as it has 3 electrons in its outer shell which it shares to form bonds. Fluorine (F) has a valency of 1, not 3, as it gains one electron to complete its octet. Therefore, both given pairs are incorrect.

Extra Facts:
Valency plays a crucial role in understanding the chemical properties of elements. Hydrogen has a valency of 1, Oxygen 2, and Nitrogen 3. Carbon has a valency of 4, enabling it to form complex compounds. Valency is determined based on the electron configuration of an element.

question:
Transition elements are the elements that are found in Groups 3-12 of the modern periodic table, that constitute the _____

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: d-block
s-block
p-block
f-block
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is d-block

Explanation:
Transition elements are those elements found in Groups 3-12 of the modern periodic table. These elements constitute the d-block because their last electron enters the d-subshell. These elements have partially filled d-orbitals, which give them unique properties such as magnetic properties, the ability to form colored compounds, and catalytic properties. Examples of transition elements include Iron (Fe), Copper (Cu), and Zinc (Zn). These elements often form metallic bonds and exhibit high melting and boiling points.

Extra Facts:
Some important properties of transition elements include their variable oxidation states, which play a crucial role in chemical reactions. These elements often act as catalysts, such as Platinum (Pt) and Nickel (Ni). Their compounds are often colored due to d-d transitions that absorb visible light. Transition elements are widely used in industrial processes, electronics, and jewelry.

question:
Identify the correct statement about Newlands' law of octaves.

options: He started with the element having the highest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at thorium which was the 56th element.
He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at sodium.
He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at aluminum.

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is d (He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass (hydrogen) and ended at thorium which was the 56th element.)

Explanation:
Newlands' Law of Octaves was an early attempt to classify elements. Newlands arranged elements in order of increasing atomic mass and observed that every eighth element had properties similar to the first, much like the octaves in music. He started with the element having the lowest atomic mass, hydrogen, and ended at thorium (the 56th element). This law worked well only up to calcium, as elements beyond this did not follow the pattern.

Extra Facts:
1. Newlands' Law of Octaves was proposed in 1865.
2. The limitation of this law was that it applied only to lighter elements and could not accommodate newly discovered elements.
3. This law was later replaced by Mendeleev's Periodic Law, which was more comprehensive and accurate.
4. Newlands was inspired by musical principles to develop this law.

question:
The atomic number of an element is the number of _______ in the nucleus of each atom of that element.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: electrons
mesons
neutrons
protons
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is protons

Explanation:
The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of protons in the nucleus of each atom of that element. This is a fundamental property that identifies the element. For example, hydrogen has an atomic number of 1, meaning it has 1 proton in its nucleus. Elements in the periodic table are arranged based on their atomic number. The number of electrons can be equal to the atomic number, but this is only true for a neutral atom, while ions may have a different number of electrons. The number of neutrons is independent of the atomic number and leads to the formation of isotopes.

Extra Facts:
The Periodic Table arranges elements based on their atomic number. Henry Moseley established the concept of atomic number in 1913. The atomic number not only identifies the element but also determines its chemical properties. The mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons. Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, resulting in different masses.

सोडियम (Na) का परमाणु द्रव्यमान 23 होता है। परमाणु द्रव्यमान किसी तत्व के एक परमाणु का द्रव्यमान होता है, जिसे एटॉमिक मास यूनिट (amu) में व्यक्त किया जाता है। सोडियम आवर्त सारणी के ग्रुप 1 (क्षार धातु) में स्थित है और इसका परमाणु क्रमांक 11 है, जिसका अर्थ है कि इसके नाभिक में 11 प्रोटॉन होते हैं। सोडियम के सबसे स्थिर आइसोटोप (Na-23) में 12 न्यूट्रॉन होते हैं, जिसके कारण इसका परमाणु द्रव्यमान 23 होता है। यह रासायनिक प्रतिक्रियाओं में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है, जैसे कि नमक (NaCl) का निर्माण।

Extra Facts:

question:
Identify the element that does NOT belong to Period 6 of Modern Periodic Table.

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Silicon
Tungsten
Rhenium
Platinum
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Silicon

Explanation:
In the modern periodic table, Period 6 includes elements with atomic numbers ranging from 55 (Caesium) to 86 (Radon). This includes Tungsten (W, atomic number 74), Rhenium (Re, atomic number 75), and Platinum (Pt, atomic number 78).

Silicon (Si, atomic number 14) belongs to Period 3 and Group 14, making it unrelated to Period 6. It is a metalloid widely used in computer chips, solar cells, and other electronic devices.

Extra Facts:
- In the periodic table, Periods are horizontal rows, while Groups are vertical columns.
- Period 6 also includes the Lanthanides (atomic numbers 57-71), often displayed separately at the bottom.
- Tungsten is used in bulb filaments due to its extremely high melting point (3422°C).
- Platinum is a precious metal used in jewelry and catalytic converters.

question:
According to Newland’s Law of Octaves, every eighth element has properties similar to those of the first element. Which of the following elements has properties similar to those of N?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: P
Al
S
B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is P

Explanation:
Newland’s Law of Octaves states that when elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic weights, every eighth element has properties similar to the first. Nitrogen (N) has an atomic number of 7. Therefore, the eighth element from N would be phosphorus (P), with an atomic number of 15 (7 + 8). Hence, P has properties similar to N. This law worked well for lighter elements but showed limitations as more elements were discovered.

Extra Facts:
1. Newland’s Law of Octaves was proposed by John Newlands in 1864.
2. It was inspired by musical octaves, where the eighth note resembles the first.
3. This law played a key role in the development of the periodic table but was accurate only up to calcium (Ca).
4. Later, Mendeleev’s Periodic Law replaced it, stating that properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

question:
Which of the following elements has variable valency?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Iron
Sodium
Sulphur
Magnesium
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Iron

Explanation:
Iron (Fe) is a transition metal that exhibits variable valency. Transition metals have incomplete d-orbitals, enabling them to show multiple valencies. Iron commonly displays two valencies: Fe²⁺ (ferrous) and Fe³⁺ (ferric). Other options like sodium (Na) always show +1, magnesium (Mg) +2, and sulphur (S) -2, +4, +6 valencies, but unlike iron, their valency is not termed 'variable' in the same context.

Extra Facts:
Variable valency is a characteristic feature of transition metals due to their partially filled d-orbitals. For example, copper (Cu) shows +1 and +2, while manganese (Mn) exhibits +2, +3, +4, +6, and +7 valencies. This property enables diverse chemical reactions and plays a crucial role in compound formation, such as in hemoglobin (Fe²⁺) and rust (Fe³⁺).

☛ What is the valency of iron in FeSO₄? → +2
☛ What is the valency of iron in Fe₂O₃? → +3
☛ Which element shows fixed valency? → Sodium (+1)

question:
In 1866, John Newlands, an English scientist, arranged the then known elements in the order of _________ . It is known as 'Newlands' Law of Octaves'.

[SSC GD 2024]
options: decreasing atomic masses
increasing atomic number
increasing atomic masses
decreasing atomic number
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is increasing atomic masses

Explanation:
John Newlands arranged the then known elements in the order of increasing atomic masses in 1866. He observed that every eighth element had similar properties, which he called 'Newlands' Law of Octaves'. This arrangement was analogous to musical octaves, where the eighth note repeats the first. However, this law worked only for lighter elements and failed for heavier ones. Later, Moseley proposed the modern periodic table based on atomic number.

Extra Facts:
Newlands' Law of Octaves was a significant step in the development of the periodic table but had limitations. It worked only up to calcium (Ca), beyond which the repetition of properties did not occur. Additionally, Newlands proposed his law before the discovery of noble gases, creating gaps in his arrangement. Later, Mendeleev developed a better periodic table based on atomic mass and chemical properties.

question:
The Law of Octaves’ was proposed by:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Alexander Newlands
Dmitri Mendeleev
Lothar Meyer
Johann Dobereiner
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Alexander Newlands

Explanation:
The 'Law of Octaves' was proposed by Alexander Newlands in 1865. According to this law, when elements are arranged in increasing order of their atomic weights, every eighth element has properties similar to the first. This is analogous to musical octaves, where the eighth note repeats the first. However, this law was applicable only up to calcium (Ca) and failed for heavier elements. Later, Mendeleev developed the Periodic Table, which was more systematic and accurate.

Extra Facts:
1. Johann Dobereiner proposed the 'Law of Triads,' where elements were grouped in threes based on similar properties.
2. Dmitri Mendeleev developed the Periodic Table and explained the periodicity of elements' properties.
3. Lothar Meyer also studied the relationship between physical properties and atomic weights of elements, but his work was parallel to Mendeleev's.

question:
Which of the following pairs of 'number - composition' is correct?
I. Atomic number - number of protons
II. Mass number - Sum of number of neutrons and protons

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Only I
Neither I nor II
Both I and II
Only II
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Both I and II

Explanation:
The atomic number represents the number of protons in an atom's nucleus and defines the element's identity and position in the periodic table. The mass number is the sum of protons and neutrons in the nucleus, expressed as: Mass Number = Number of Protons + Number of Neutrons. Thus, both statements I and II are correct.

Extra Facts:
Understanding the difference between atomic and mass numbers is crucial. The atomic number determines an element's chemical properties, while the mass number helps identify its isotopes. Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers due to varying neutron counts. For example, Carbon-12 and Carbon-14 both have an atomic number of 6, but mass numbers of 12 and 14, respectively.

question:
Which of the following is a non-metal that can exist in different form?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Mercury
Carbon
Lithium
Potassium
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Carbon

Explanation:
Carbon is a non-metal that exists in different forms called allotropes. Its major allotropes include Diamond, Graphite, and Fullerene. Diamond is the hardest natural substance, while Graphite conducts electricity, and Fullerene is used in nanotechnology. These variations arise due to carbon's tetravalency and covalent bonding. Other options like Mercury, Lithium, and Potassium are metals and do not exhibit allotropy.

Extra Facts:
Allotropy refers to the existence of an element in multiple physical forms. Besides carbon, Phosphorus (red, white, black), Sulfur (rhombic, monoclinic), and Oxygen (O₂, O₃) also show allotropy. New carbon allotropes like nanotubes and graphene are significant in modern research.

[SSC MTS 2022]

कार्बन
लीथियम
पोटैशियम
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है कार्बन

Explanation:
कार्बन एक अधातु है जो विभिन्न रूपों (allotropes) में पाया जाता है। इसके कुछ प्रमुख अपरूप हैं: हीरा (Diamond), ग्रेफाइट (Graphite), और फुलरीन (Fullerene)। हीरा सबसे कठोर प्राकृतिक पदार्थ है, जबकि ग्रेफाइट विद्युत का सुचालक है और फुलरीन नैनोटेक्नोलॉजी में उपयोगी है। कार्बन के ये विभिन्न रूप इसकी संयोजकता (Tetravalency) और बंधन प्रकृति (Covalent Bonding) के कारण संभव होते हैं। अन्य विकल्प जैसे पारा (Mercury), लीथियम (Lithium), और पोटैशियम (Potassium) धातुएँ हैं और इनमें अपरूपता नहीं पाई जाती।

Extra Facts:
अपरूपता (Allotropy) एक ही तत्व के विभिन्न भौतिक रूपों में पाए जाने की घटना है। कार्बन के अलावा, फॉस्फोरस (लाल, सफेद, काला), सल्फर (रोम्बिक, मोनोक्लिनिक), और ऑक्सीजन (O₂, O₃) भी अपरूपता प्रदर्शित करते हैं। कार्बन के नैनोट्यूब और ग्राफीन जैसे नए अपरूप भी वैज्ञानिक शोध में महत्वपूर्ण हैं।

question:
Identify whether the given statements about p-block elements are correct or incorrect.
Statement A: In p-block elements, the last electron enters the outermost p orbital.
Statement B: The non-metals and metalloids exist only in the p-block of the periodic table.

[SSC CPO 2023]
options: Both Statements A and B are correct
Only Statement A is correct
Only Statement B is correct
Both Statements A and B are incorrect
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Both Statements A and B are correct

Explanation:
Statement A: In p-block elements, the last electron enters the outermost p orbital. This statement is correct because the defining feature of p-block elements is that their last electron fills the p-orbital. These elements are found in groups 13 to 18 of the periodic table.

Statement B: Non-metals and metalloids exist only in the p-block of the periodic table. This statement is also correct because non-metals (e.g., oxygen, nitrogen) and metalloids (e.g., boron, silicon) are exclusively found in the p-block. Other blocks (s, d, f) primarily contain metals.

Extra Facts:
The p-block exhibits great diversity, including noble gases (group 18). It also contains biologically significant elements like oxygen, nitrogen, and carbon. These elements are crucial in industrial and biological processes.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ How many blocks are there in the periodic table? → 4 (s, p, d, f)
☛ Which group in the p-block contains noble gases? → Group 18
☛ What type of element is boron? → Metalloid
☛ Which block does carbon belong to? → p-block
☛ In which block is hydrogen located in the periodic table? → s-block

p-ब्लॉक के तत्वों के बारे में दिए गए सही या गलत कथनों की पहचान कीजिए।
कथन A: p-ब्लॉक तत्वों में, अंतिम इलेक्ट्रॉन वाह्यतम p कक्षक में प्रवेश करता है।
कथन B: अधातुएं और उपधातुएं केवल आवर्त सारणी के p-ब्लॉक में मौजूद होती हैं।

[SSC CPO 2023]
options_hi: कथन A और B दोनों सही हैं
केवल कथन A सही है
केवल कथन B सही है
कथन A और B दोनों गलत हैं
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है कथन A और B दोनों सही हैं

Explanation:
कथन A: p-ब्लॉक तत्वों में, अंतिम इलेक्ट्रॉन वाह्यतम p कक्षक में प्रवेश करता है। यह कथन सही है क्योंकि p-ब्लॉक तत्वों की परिभाषा ही यह है कि इनमें अंतिम इलेक्ट्रॉन p-कक्षक में भरता है। ये तत्व आवर्त सारणी के समूह 13 से 18 तक पाए जाते हैं।

कथन B: अधातुएं और उपधातुएं केवल आवर्त सारणी के p-ब्लॉक में मौजूद होती हैं। यह कथन भी सही है क्योंकि अधातुएं (जैसे ऑक्सीजन, नाइट्रोजन) और उपधातुएं (जैसे बोरॉन, सिलिकॉन) केवल p-ब्लॉक में ही पाई जाती हैं। अन्य ब्लॉक (s, d, f) में मुख्य रूप से धातुएं होती हैं।

Extra Facts:
p-ब्लॉक तत्वों में विविधता अधिक होती है। इनमें अक्रिय गैसें (नॉबल गैस) भी शामिल हैं, जो समूह 18 में स्थित हैं। p-ब्लॉक तत्वों में ऑक्सीजन, नाइट्रोजन, कार्बन जैसे जैविक रूप से महत्वपूर्ण तत्व भी शामिल हैं। इन तत्वों का उपयोग अनेक औद्योगिक और जैविक प्रक्रियाओं में होता है।
